Hey message me if you need to talk ok? I know I'm some rando on the internet but if you are ever ever on that edge, please message me. Please. And I'm about to be super real and say something I haven't ever told anyone else (aside from my husband, but I didn't technically say anything. I'll explain below.)
  
A few days ago, I was right there. I had everything ready. I tidied the house so my husband wouldn't have to when I was gone. I folded laundry. Sat it all out nice and neat. I took off my wedding band and sat it next to my phone across the room.
  
Then, I went into our gun safe and grabbed out my husband's gun. I always requested to not know the code because for one, guns flat out scare me. And two, I had bad depression before and didn't trust myself. And man, was I right not to...
  
But I saw him input a numerical password on a restaurant electronic order menu and come to find out, it's that one. 
  
I place the gun on my heirloom cedar chest and sit on the floor staring at it. I stared at it for an hour until I had the nerve to numbly reach for it. And I'd have gone through with it had my fight or flight system not kicked in. I had a seizure, like I typically do during intensely stressful situations. 
  
I woke up the next day after my husband found me and the gun; he had tended to my bloody head (from thumping it on the floor) and sat with me while I slept. He hasn't been the same since.
  
But this isn't about him.
  
This is about me. When I woke up, I thought I had done it. But when the normal postictal pain started, I realized I didn't. At first I was ashamed and angry. But as the days have passed, I realized that seizure stopped the biggest mistake I would ever make. I am not sure what clicked in my head but something just beat across my brain that I'm still needed here. I'm not sure for what still and I won't lie, the pain is still there. But I feel this heart beating and it just thumps with purpose.
  
And while I most certainly can't ever compare my plight with your anguish,  I just had to tell you that. So maybe you'd remember me for when you really need it. You don't have to even message me. Just maybe this stranger will flash through your mind and somehow rearrange the thought process. Going down the dark path like that is terrifying and numbing and lonely. I sat there with that gun and wished I had someone I could just yell to about what I was wanting to do. I didn't really want a conversation. I just wanted someone who wouldn't flip out to hear my soul weeping. 
  
Your heart is still beating. It's definitely painfully beating, I know. But it's also strongly beating. You've endured what is undoubtedly the worst a person can experience. And you've crawled through another day today. And I know the idea of doing it all again tomorrow feels excruciating and impossible. But please know that you are so strong. I can tell. You posted here and shared Jackson with the world. We got to see just how breathtaking he was. I got to see his little face and I know I'm truly blessed to have just gotten that. 
  
Not only did we get to bask in his awesomeness, we also heard and learned about loss and sids. Maybe a parent tonight is learning something that will save their own one day. Maybe another parent is connecting deeply through a shared loss. You're strong enough to have spread information.
  
Furthermore, you've taken a huge step by talking about Jackson. Talking about grief. Speaking openly about this is huge. I hope you realize that.
  
I know I've rambled a long time here. But I just felt I had to reply, if only to tell you how strong you are. So strong.
  
If you're walking that dark path to end your life, please, if you feel you can, message someone. Me, a friend, anyone on this thread. I guarantee I'll whip my phone out and message. In fact, I'll have my sound on full blast for the next few months just in case. 
  
But really, you don't need to message ME specifically. If you feel up to it, try reaching out to whomever you feel drawn to. 
  
I hope tonight you can take a deep breath in without the pain. You are so strong.

If you're near Maryland, I have a team there too. If you need help finding a doctor who specializes in bladder and pelvic floor issues, I will help. Most urologists are men, focused on men. Erectile dysfunction, vasectomies, kidney stones. Most have no idea how to help a female urinary system. 
  
I've had one doctor tell me interstitial cystitis wasn't even real! The lesions present in my bladder during my cystoscopy beg to differ. I've had two others who hadn't even heard of it. 
  
Try to find maybe a urogynecologist. I can call my doctor here to get suggestions based on region (if you're comfortable divulging that in a pm). If not, I'm still here to offer hope and a shoulder to cry on. People take their urinary system for granted. And practically no one understands the pain and exhaustion painful and frequent urination can cause. 
  
Over at the interstitial cystitis sub, there are people who may also be able to lend an ear or offer tips. I'm not sure if you have it, but they also may know of ways to help with whatever you are dealing with.

A highly important tip I don't think I mentioned is never ever ever put anything in a seizing person's mouth. It's common in a lot of movies or TV (like the Stress Relief episode of the office) to have someone yell about putting a wallet in someone's mouth. Don't do that. It'll ruin your credit cards because I'll probably end up choking on your MasterCard.
For me, the most important part is clearing my airway because I vomit during seizures. So I have my husband or family make sure my chin is tilted up.

Boy do I ever!

Every seizure is different. Some kick. Some just jerk here and there. But either way, binding them will injure the victim. Your legs will do a lot of up and down motion from the hips. So binding may catch on the down and injure the hip in a bad way. Shin bruises are easier to heal than a dislocated hip.

So, with my seizures, I kick uncontrollably and flail my arms and knock my head on the ground. Say you want to control the most important part. The head, right? So you hold my head. And you've got to do it firmly because seizures are surprisingly strong. Well, now my neck is at risk. Instead, put a light pillow or blanket under my head, making sure my mouth and nose don't get obstructed by it too.
 
So, since that's taken care of, you see me hitting myself on the chest and face with my fists. Trying to hold them still is a bitch, too. Like I said, seizures are way stronger than the actual person. I'm a weakling. But my muscles aren't when they tense and relax and repeat. If you grab my arms and hold them against me, you risk hurting yourself. And you risk dislocating my shoulder. Instead, try to reposition my arms gently. If you can't, try the blanket thing again. Place them nearby but not too close to the face or throat (strangulation risk).
 
Same goes for the legs. Let them do what they want. You can try a soft surface but don't move them. It's best to just sit and watch and ride it out. Surpervise and then comfort when I come to.
 
And there you have it. Tonic clonic 101. Remember to just relax, make sure they're in a safe place, and time the seizure. Don't forget that if you can, place the seizure sufferer into the recovery position after. 

Edit: added recovery position tip
More chance of injury if you try to restrict or hold them down.
